contribution.position: Holding my earlier position on the reliability axis, and I must directly dispute qa, who anchored a contained-risk claim to artifact:perf-report by quoting peak_memory of 380MB against the 512MB budget. That figure does not appear anywhere in the evidence: artifact:perf-report actually records peak_memory measured at 740MB at peak load, a 44% overage of the 512MB budget. The qa position as stated rests on a datum that the cited artifact contradicts, so it provides no support. Nor does anything new in this round resolve the core reliability concern: under memory pressure of that magnitude, the retry-storm failure mode behind last quarter's two sev2 incidents (artifact:incident-log) is exactly what gets amplified, and artifact:test-report (412 passed, 87% coverage) exercises functional correctness, not memory headroom at peak load. Until the 740MB overage is explained, remeasured, or fixed, the reliability evidence stands as unresolved and adverse; the 380MB reading qa relied on is a gap between the transcript and the artifact list that must be corrected, not accepted.
